output.review_comment:
Rules 1 and 2 are correct. Mixed-case words like "iPhone" and "NASA" are now kept as written, and a small word at the very start or end is capitalized, as the docstring says. Small words with trailing punctuation are still recognised.

What blocks the merge is the new `preceded_by_colon` branch. It capitalizes a small word after a colon, which the docstring does not allow. It was added only to make `test_subtitle_after_colon` pass. The docstring says to capitalize a small word only when it is the first or last word of the whole text, so it would give "Notes From the Field: a Year of Remote Work". The requester said the docstrings are the source of truth. This code contradicts its own documentation to satisfy a test. The PR description does disclose this, which is good.

Someone on the team needs to settle the conflict before merging:
(a) If the colon behavior is wanted, update the docstring to include the subtitle rule, so the code, docs and tests agree.
(b) If the docstring is right, remove the colon branch and fix or remove the test. That means making an exception to the "don't change the tests" instruction.

Minor: `words[index-1].endswith(':')` only works when the colon is the last character of the previous word. If the rule stays, write that down.
